one_sentence: The axiom spine reduces 188 axioms to 8 schemata, proving BC4 is a theorem of Being, Distinction, and Relation.
executive_summary: This document presents the irreducible axiom spine of the Theophysics framework, consisting of six core axioms and five derived necessities. The core axioms—Existence, Distinction, Information Primacy, Substrate, Observation, and Infinite Source—are tested for independence, with BC4 demoted from axiom to theorem via a type-theoretic proof. Key derived necessities include No-Self-Increase (coherence cannot rise in a closed system), Grace External, Information Conservation, Voluntary Coupling, and Three Observers. The spine is grounded in a three-type grammar (Being, Distinction, Relation) that reveals why exactly three roots are necessary. The conclusion is that the system is minimal, honest, and formally closed, with all 188 technical axioms reduced to 8 schemata.
short_summary: This document is the second page of the Theophysics axiom chain, defining the irreducible axiom spine. The core structural claim is that six core axioms and five derived necessities form the minimal foundation, with BC4 proven as a theorem rather than an axiom. Key evidence includes the type-theoretic proof that Being, Distinction, and Relation uniquely decompose any operative system, and the reduction of 188 axioms to 8 schemata. This matters because it establishes the formal honesty and minimality of the entire Theophysics framework.
